---
title: "Embedded documentation"
description: "Read the Quarto 2 documentation straight from the q2 binary, with no network access: in a browser with `q2 docs serve`, or as markdown for AI agents with `q2 docs llms`."
---

## Overview

Every `q2` binary carries this documentation site inside it, and it is
the documentation for **the version of Quarto you are running**, not
whatever the website currently says. There are two ways to read it,
both offline:

- `q2 docs serve` opens the full site — navigation, search, and the
  embedded examples — in your web browser.
- `q2 docs llms` prints a markdown copy for AI coding agents and other
  tools that prefer plain text.

## Reading the docs in a browser

```bash
q2 docs serve
```

starts a small web server on your machine for the embedded site and
opens it in your browser. `q2 docs open` does exactly the same thing;
use whichever name you remember. Press Ctrl-C to stop the server.

To jump straight to a page, name it. Any spelling that
[`q2 docs llms`](#fetching-a-page) accepts works here too:

```bash
q2 docs open guides/projects/preview
q2 docs open errors                     # the error-code index
```

The server reads everything from the binary; nothing is downloaded.
(The one exception is cosmetic: if you are online, the browser fetches
the site's Source Sans Pro font from Google Fonts, just as it would on
the public website. Offline, text uses your system's sans-serif font.)

Use `--port` to pick the port, `--no-browser` to just print the URL,
and `--browser` to open a specific browser. `--host` changes the
network interface; the default, `127.0.0.1`, keeps the server private
to your machine.

## Documentation for AI agents

AI coding agents — and any tool that prefers plain text to rendered
HTML — can read the markdown copy directly from the command line:

```bash
q2 docs llms
```

That prints an index of every documentation page, in the
[llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format. The index is small enough to
paste into a prompt; each entry names a page you can then fetch on
demand.

The docs are the ones this site was built from, so an agent reading
them is reading documentation for **the version of Quarto it is
actually running** — not whatever it remembers, and not a newer or
older website.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Point your agent here

If you use an AI coding assistant, telling it once that
`q2 docs llms` exists is usually enough. Many agents will then
discover the pages they need without further help.
:::

### Fetching a page

Each entry in the index is an href. Pass one to fetch that page's
markdown:

```bash
q2 docs llms guides/authoring/figures.md
```

Paths are forgiving: the `.qmd` and `.html` spellings of a page work
too, as does leaving the extension off entirely, and naming a
directory gets you its index page.

```bash
q2 docs llms guides/authoring/figures      # same page
q2 docs llms guides/authoring              # the section's index
```

If a path doesn't match anything, `q2` suggests near matches and exits
with an error rather than printing nothing.

### Listing every page

```bash
q2 docs llms --list
```

prints one line per page — the href, a tab, and the page title — which
is the convenient form for scripts and for agents that want to search
titles before fetching:

```
guides/authoring/figures.md	Figures
guides/authoring/tables.md	Tables
guides/projects/llms-txt.md	llms.txt: a markdown mirror for AI tools
```

### Machine-readable JSON

Programs that consume the page list or the provenance report can read
them as JSON instead of parsing the text forms:

```bash
q2 docs llms --list --json
q2 docs llms --embed-info --json
```

`--list --json` prints a `[{"href": "...", "title": "..."}, ...]` array
in the same order as the text form; `--embed-info --json` prints
`{"placeholder": false, "commit": "...", "dirty": false, "pages": 255}`.
`--json` works only with `--list` or `--embed-info`.

### The whole corpus at once

```bash
q2 docs llms --full
```

concatenates every page into a single stream. It is far too large for
most models to read in one prompt — expect several hundred kilobytes —
but it is the right input for building a search index, a vector store,
or any other downstream tool that wants everything at once.

## Which docs are embedded?

```bash
q2 docs llms --embed-info
```

reports where the embedded snapshot came from:

```
source: real
commit: e3b3d7d4aae422274a7f3ff1c781019c24bfbb07
pages: 255
```

Released binaries always carry the documentation built from that
release's source. A `q2` you built yourself may report
`source: placeholder`, meaning no documentation was embedded; the
command tells you how to build and embed it. `q2 docs serve` and
`q2 docs llms` read the same embedded snapshot, so this report covers
both.

## Related

- [llms.txt: a markdown mirror for AI tools](projects/llms-txt.qmd)
  publishes the same kind of markdown mirror for **your own**
  website. `q2 docs llms` is that feature turned on Quarto's own
  documentation and shipped inside the binary.
- `q2 agents-info` is an alias for `q2 docs llms` — the two are
  interchangeable.
